summary.headline: JG Chemicals posted record Q2 FY27 revenue of INR361.01 crore (+64% YoY) and PAT of INR27.95 crore (+86% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 10.71%.
summary.overview: Management reported its best-ever quarter, with revenue, EBITDA and PAT all at new quarterly highs, driven by tire and rubber demand and a favourable product mix. H1 FY27 revenue rose 54% to INR676.66 crore and PAT rose 72% to INR54.07 crore. Sequentially, EBITDA margin eased from 11.50% in Q1 to 10.71% in Q2, which management attributed to raw material cost lags. Capacity additions at Dahej (trial runs next month) and Naidupeta (now mid-January 2027 commissioning) remain the main growth levers.

segments.name: Zinc oxide (tire and rubber)
segments.commentary: Principal market; management says it is the largest zinc oxide supplier to the tire industry. Q2 volume growth was in the mid-teens, and the company says it has surplus capacity for the next 6 to 9 months.

segments.name: Non-rubber applications
segments.commentary: Over 18% of sales in H1 FY27, up from close to 10% in FY24, spanning ceramics, specialty chemicals, agriculture and pharma. Target is about 30% in the next 2 to 3 years.

segments.name: Zinc sulphate
segments.commentary: Installed capacity of 10,000 MTPA at Naidupeta, utilisation about 50%; contributes under 3% of revenue, expected at 5% to 7% share over time.

guidance_outlook: Dahej Phase 1 (about 15,000 MTPA zinc oxide): trial runs next month (December 2026), followed by customer qualification and ramp-up.
Naidupeta brownfield (about 5,000 MTPA): slipped from Q3 to mid-to-end January 2027 commissioning; earlier management said Q4 FY27.
Total zinc oxide capacity to rise to about 79,900 TPA after both projects; management says this covers demand through FY28 and FY29. Dahej Phase 2 expected to start around mid-to-late 2028.
Dahej utilisation targeted at about 60% to 70% in FY28.
Consolidated EBITDA margin targeted at 14% to 15% in about 3 years; management says the current level is sustainable.
Internal target to double revenue every 3 years; management expects FY27 revenue well above INR1,200 crore.
Dahej revenue potential of about INR900 crore now expected around FY29 to FY30, with peak potential said to be higher.
Net cash expected above INR100 crore at FY27 end; no borrowing expected even if H1 revenue doubles.
capex_capacity: Dahej greenfield (Gujarat): Phase 1 about 15,000 MTPA of a planned 40,000-plus MTPA facility; trial runs next month.
Naidupeta brownfield: about 5,000 MTPA addition; commissioning mid-January 2027.
Post both projects, installed capacity to be over 115,000 tons of zinc chemicals, per management.
Acquired about 16.74 acres of freehold land at Naidupeta (Tirupati District, Andhra Pradesh) through BDJ Oxides Private Limited for future expansion.
Zinc sulphate: 10,000 MTPA installed; some new zinc sulphate products expected in FY28, with details to be shared in early 2027.
Naidupeta solar Phase 1 operational, meeting about 25% to 30% of energy needs; payback about 4 years. Further capacity under evaluation after new government regulations from 1 January.
JG TUR (Tire Upscaled Rubber, recycled rubber): pilot trials successful with key customers; full-scale venture being planned, with capex and timeline to be shared later.
demand_pricing: Q2 volume growth in the mid-teens; management expects Q3 numbers to exceed the current run rate, and October was the highest production month to date.

Indian auto volumes in Q2: passenger vehicles about 30% YoY, two-wheelers about 15%, commercial vehicles about 29%, three-wheelers about 23%. Indian tire majors have about INR25,000 crore of announced capex.
Raw material: over 100 global suppliers. Margin dip QoQ attributed to lag between LME-linked purchase cost and selling price, plus longer lead times from West Asia disruption.
Management says the West Asia cost increase was passed on to customers in Q1 and has already been absorbed.

Industry consolidation: management says customers are shifting volumes from small zinc oxide producers (70% to 80% of India's producers) to larger players, and expects some business reallocated to JG over 5 to 7 years.
Pricing: management says it is agnostic to zinc price, since selling price follows the prior month's LME average. Per-ton price may fall if zinc falls, but volume growth is the focus.
Battery-grade zinc oxide: JG is the only Indian producer benchmarked and approved under an international zinc battery initiative; volumes expected in 2 to 3 years, high-margin, low volume.

qa_highlights.question: What was the volume growth in Q2, and why did gross margin fall about 130 bps QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth was in the mid-teens. Management said gross margin moves with inventory lead and lag, and it focuses on EBITDA and per-ton margin instead. It sees a blended EBITDA margin of 14% to 15% within about 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative in H1 FY27, and will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is 90 to 100 days. Management said March inventory was low due to shipping delays from the West Asia crisis, and that cash should be significantly higher at 31 March. Debtor days are in line with history.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall QoQ, and was the procurement discount on dross and ash changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed a time lag: lower-cost material bought at lower LME prices arrived late, while higher-cost domestic material hit plants first. Management expects this to average out by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Dahej timeline, Phase 2 start, and the sustainability of non-rubber growth and margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 is expected around mid-to-late 2028. Specialty grades for pharma, cosmetics and specialty chemicals are expected to lift margins more than ceramics. Blended EBITDA is expected to move toward 14%.

qa_highlights.question: Is demand sustainable into Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tire demand is strong, with OEM and replacement demand both firm. It expects no demand aberration given 7% to 8% economic growth, and says Dahej should help with ceramics, which has a low base.

qa_highlights.question: Dahej utilisation, tire versus non-tire mix, and ceramics target?
qa_highlights.answer: Dahej utilisation is targeted at about 60% to 70% in FY28. Management aims for 10% to 15% of the ceramics market, against over 30% share in India overall, and notes two large tire plants about 5 km from Dahej.

risks_watch: Naidupeta commissioning has slipped from Q3 to mid-January 2027; Dahej trial runs and customer qualification timing must hold.
Working capital is heavy (inventory rose from INR92 crore in March to INR154 crore in September; receivables from INR177 crore to INR207 crore), and H1 operating cash flow was negative.
Quarterly EBITDA margin volatility from LME pricing lags and West Asia-related lead times.
Ceramics demand was hit by West Asia gas issues, and the ramp-up depends on the Dahej market.
Recycled rubber (JG TUR) and battery-grade zinc oxide still at pilot or qualification stage with no quantified revenue.
Zinc sulphate utilisation about 50%, with ramp-up dependent on new specialised grades.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, capacity and margins, with management repeatedly calling Q2 a record. It was more defensive on the sequential margin dip and negative operating cash flow, attributing both to timing and inventory lags. Specific timelines (Naidupeta, Dahej Phase 2, FY28 zinc sulphate launches) were given loosely or deferred.
key_quotes: JG delivered its best ever quarterly performance in the current Q2 FY27, surpassing the previous record achieved in the Q1.
JGC is India's largest zinc recycling company and a leading manufacturer of zinc oxide, a value-added green chemical, today manufactured using recycled zinc.
So if you see quarter-on-quarter, you will see a slight dip in the EBITDA margins.
I think at the end of the year, it averages out.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue well above INR1,200 crore (H1 FY27 was INR676.66 crore), backed by Dahej Phase 1 (15,000 MTPA, trial runs December 2026) and Naidupeta 5,000 MTPA (slipped to mid-January 2027), with utilisation above 80% and mid-teens Q2 volume growth; Naidupeta timing slippage tempers confidence.
